reporting-org.narrative: Organisation des Nations unies pour l'éducation, la science et la culture (UNESCO)
United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

description.narrative:
The current characteristics of the digital ecosystem have facilitated, in an unprecedented scale, the information flow and the enjoyment of human rights, but disinformation campaigns and several forms of harmful content are causing societal polarization and eroding democratic institutions. Global consensus calls for improved digital platform governance, ensuring human rights due diligence, content moderation and content curation with a human rights-based approach, transparency, accountability, user empowerment, and independent oversight. UNESCO has developed, through a multistakeholder process, Guidelines for the governance of digital platforms (“the Guidelines”) to ensure that everyone's freedom of expression, access to information and diverse cultural content are fully guaranteed, while various stakeholders, including Member States, deal with key problems in the digital ecosystem, including dis- and misinformation and hate speech online.
Thus, this project aims to safeguard and foster freedom of expression and access to information in the context of digital platform governance. To achieve this objective, UNESCO will promote a global understanding of a human rights-based approach of digital platform governance, which includes the improvement of practices and capacities of public sector as well as stronger advocacy and watchdog roles of civil society. A comparative perspective with other ongoing governance processes, such as the European Union Digital Services Act, will also complement the overall strategy of the project.
The scope of the project will be limited to sub-regions of Africa, Asia and the Pacific and Latin America and the Caribbean to narrow the asymmetries between several actors, including governments, in governing the digital platforms.
